title: Entropy-aware batching probe notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal notebook for an experiment: use a lightweight per-request entropy signal to reduce batching inefficiencies and KV-cache churn during inference.

Background / motivation:
- Problem: current batching groups requests mostly by arrival time and token length heuristics. This leads to:
  * high variance batches where some requests produce very peaky attention (high entropy) causing longer decode time and cache thrash;
  * wasted tokens when we batch low-entropy short-turn requests with high-entropy long-turn ones;
  * poorer tail latency for bursty multi-tenant workloads.
- Hypothesis: a simple per-request "entropy score" (quick approximation) can be used to gate batching or form affinity groups that improve throughput and tail latency without harming average cost.

Entropy estimator ideas (cheap):
- token-unigram-entropy: precompute per-token log-prob from unigram table of training corpus (very cheap) -> sum/average per-request;
- tokenizer-perplexity-proxy: run small 64-token LM on prefix (micro LM) to estimate perplexity — heavier but still <1ms for small models on CPU;
- token-shannon-sum: approximate by token id distribution entropy on prompt slots (for prompts with many tokens this approximates diversity).

Core config knobs to prototype (API / runtime fields):
- batch_policy: "entropy_affinity" | "entropy_threshold" | "none"
- entropy_estimator: "unigram" | "micro-lm" | "token-shannon"
- affinity_window_ms: integer (max time to wait to collect affinity group)
- max_affinity_group_size: integer (max requests in same entropy bin)
- entropy_bins: comma list floats e.g. "0.0,1.0,2.5,4.0" (buckets used for affinity grouping)
- entropy_threshold_ms_tradeoff: JSON-ish string to tune waiting time vs latency (see experiments)
- fallback_policy: "time-bound" | "size-bound" | "mixed"

Example runtime config (as note, not final schema):
- batch_policy: entropy_affinity
- entropy_estimator: unigram
- affinity_window_ms: 12
- max_affinity_group_size: 16
- entropy_bins: [0.0, 1.2, 2.8, 5.0]
- fallback_policy: mixed

How it works (rough):
1) on ingress, compute estimator(entropy) for request R -> s in real numbers.
2) map s to a bin B.
3) place R into pending queue under bin B; each bin has its own micro-window W_B (derived from affinity_window_ms and bin-specific urgency multiplier).
4) when either size-bound or time-bound triggers, emit batch for that bin.
5) runtime schedules batch with kernel/quantization variant selected by expected sequence-length-distribution + bin-specific flags (e.g., preferring cached KV reuse for low-entropy bins).

Why affinity/binning helps:
- low-entropy requests are usually deterministic, produce short incremental decode paths and share many active attention keys -> they coalesce well and benefit from continuous KV reuse;
- high-entropy requests often diverge in token next-token distribution, causing more expensive per-token compute and less benefit from grouping with low-entropy ones;
- grouping by entropy reduces tail variance and improves cache hit locality.

Metrics / telemetry to collect (minimal):
- per-bin: avg_entropy, p50/p95/p99 latency (decode-only and end-to-end), tokens-per-request, batch_size_histogram;
- KV-cache hit rate by bin;
- model-kernel utilization by bin;
- cost-per-token and cost-per-request by bin;
- rejection/fallbacks triggered (requests that waited > latency_slo and were force-batched).

Experiment matrix (quick plan):
- baseline: current time-window batching (12ms) + length bucketing.
- run A: entropy_affinity (unigram), affinity_window_ms=12, max_group=16.
- run B: entropy_affinity (micro-lm), affinity_window_ms=8, max_group=12.
- run C: entropy_threshold: if entropy > 3.5 -> immediate flush; else normal batching.
- compare under two workloads:
  * synthetic: 30% high-entropy requests (simulated by random prompts), 70% low-entropy; burst arrival distribution (poisson with bursts).
  * production-sampled: 48h sampled traffic from tenant X (anon).

Success criteria (quick):
- p95 latency decreases >= 10% for tenant X at same token cost;
- no >2% increase in mean cost per token across mixed tenants;
- KV-cache hit rate increase for low-entropy bin by >= 15%.

Open questions / caveats (notes to self):
- how to compute estimator cheaply inside Libra/ingress path with low overhead? need microbenchmarks for unigram table lookup on hot path.
- risk: an adversarial client could craft low-entropy-looking prefixes to get preferential batching (multi-tenant fairness issue). Need per-tenant gating and quota-aware affinity.
- does affinity binning interact badly with priority queues / tenant QoS? probably need to overlay tenant-priority preemptions.
- interaction with caching: if we group low-entropy requests we might increase dedup hits -> good, but must ensure KV cache doesn't evict important shards.

Proto pseudo-code (very rough):
- on_ingress(req):
    s = estimate_entropy(req.input)
    bin = find_bin(s, cfg.entropy_bins)
    queue_enqueue(bin, req)
    if queue_size(bin) >= cfg.max_affinity_group_size or time_since_first(bin) >= W_bin:
       emit_batch(bin)

- emit_batch(bin):
    batch = queue_pop_up_to(bin, cfg.max_affinity_group_size)
    schedule(batch, preferred_kernel_for(bin, batch))

Telemetry dashboard skeleton (in words):
- heatmap: bin vs hour -> avg latency / batch_size / tokens-per-batch
- stacked lines: p50/p95/p99 latency by bin over last 7d
- table: per-tenant delta vs baseline (cost, p95)

Implementation notes / next steps:
- prototype estimator module in rust shim at ingress (fast unigram lookup via mmap table).
- add config flags to routing layer to enable entropy_affinity for canary tenants.
- instrument runtime to tag requests with bin metadata for tracing.
- run synthetic microbench in sandbox cluster, collect metrics, iterate.

Small ascii diagram (flow):
  client -> ingress w/estimator -> bin queues [low|mid|high] -> micro-window -> batch scheduler -> runtime kernels -> model decode -> response

Quick TODO (self):

Notes: throwaway heuristics okay for first pass. Keep config reversible (ability to disable affinity immediately by feature flag).
